sobre.titulo: To constellate, to map, to imagine
sobre.p1: Memorias Vivas (EC-649) is a repository still taking shape. It gathers audio, video, photography, and writing that record encounters, walks, workshops, and conversations with people who live in the territories around the Golfo Dulce. It is meant as a platform for collective imagination, mutual recognition, and the defense of the territories that make life possible.
sobre.p2: The material is arranged as a constellation: a way of imagining conversations, pasts, projections, images, routes, and processes through points of contact that, once linked, let figures appear. Just as we draw imaginary lines between stars to find our way in the sky and to picture stories, affections, and destinies, scattered memories are joined here to produce new forms of recognition.
sobre.p3: The constellation works as both method and medium. It makes proximities and resonances visible and, like memory, it plays with remnants, times, and places. In that montage, relations appear among people, stories, rivers, species, climates, and infrastructures, understood not as isolated elements but as living webs that produce meaning. Each record, walk, conversation, photograph, or sound is a trace that, set beside others, opens new readings of the territories and of the lives that sustain them.
sobre.p4: The points of these constellations are made of microhistories: life stories of everyday, family, and community experience. These stories, often left out of official accounts, let us pay attention to other ways of thinking national communities and their foreignness. The project draws lines between daily experience, family memory, stories of naturecultures, and processes of inequality, slow violence, and extractivism. It does not aim for a total narrative. It attends to gestures, voices, and the ways memory and life testimony build a future, or offer clues about how to live better. In that sense, constellation is a practice of montage: it gathers scattered fragments into new forms of perception and meaning, across different media and points of view.
sobre.p5: We hope the people who use this site can imagine and trace links among uneven times, heterotopias, affections, landscapes, and experiences that rarely appear together in dominant narratives.
sobre.p6: Memories do more than reread the past. They also make it possible to imagine other ways of living and of understanding reality, ways that include other forms of imagination and more inclusive futures for other forms of life. Care among people, among species of flora and fauna, for rivers, and for the infrastructures that sustain life is vital to this process.
sobre.p7: To constellate is to recognize that there are many ways of inhabiting a territory, of relating to a place, and of building communities in times that are not linear. It means attending to transgenerational networks and to the ways they survive, change, or shift in everyday practice, in affection, and in local forms of knowledge.
